archetypes.description: Operator profiles oriented to full-service or upper-upscale hotel management with stated CALA or Mexico/Caribbean market depth.
archetypes.bestUseCase: May be relevant when the deal is in CALA and the owner is reviewing regional execution depth for full-service or resort-leaning assets.
alignmentSignals: Potential alignment when the recorded market is in CALA and the deal contemplates third-party or brand-plus-operator execution.
May be relevant if pre-opening, conversion, or repositioning increases the need for regional operating infrastructure.
Alignment signal strengthens when the owner has indicated a regional operator profile preference.
reviewConsiderations: Confirm whether required market coverage is gateway cities only or includes secondary resorts.
Review bilingual reporting, labor, and F&B complexity against stated operator capability priorities.
Validate owner expectations for centralized vs. property-level decision rights.
questionsToClarify: Which countries and sub-markets must have active operations versus pipeline-only presence?
Is the owner seeking full hotel management or a narrower commercial platform?
How does the owner define full-service scope for this asset (F&B, groups, resort amenities)?
dataGaps: Deal intake does not include a dedicated CALA operator category separate from generic Regional.
Operator-side country lists are not normalized in the current setup schema for profile-level matching.
suggestedWorkflowActions: Suggested workflow action: confirm country and Primary Market Region before comparing regional CALA operator profiles.
Suggested workflow action: align on full-service scope and reporting package before outreach.

archetypes.displayLabel: International Third-Party Manager with Market Presence
archetypes.description: Operator profiles with multi-market or international third-party management positioning and stated portfolio scale.
archetypes.bestUseCase: May be relevant when the owner is open to internationally affiliated third-party management with defined market presence requirements.
alignmentSignals: Potential alignment when third-party management or brand-plus-operator paths are under review.
May be relevant if the owner selected an international or national operator profile preference.
Alignment signal may apply across non-US markets when execution scale and brand portfolio breadth matter.
reviewConsiderations: Distinguish global brand affiliation from local third-party execution capability.
Review whether the deal requires existing market operations versus expansion appetite only.
Compare owner reporting frequency with operator governance narratives.
questionsToClarify: Which markets must have stabilized operations versus development pipeline only?
Is the owner prioritizing brand portfolio breadth or local GM-led execution?
What deal structure (management, franchise, lease) is actually under consideration?
dataGaps: International on the deal form does not confirm CALA or country-specific operator depth.
Profile-level matching does not yet evaluate named operator companies.
suggestedWorkflowActions: Suggested workflow action: document required markets and deal structure before shortlisting international operator profiles.
Suggested workflow action: validate reporting and commercial platform expectations in writing.

archetypes.description: Operator profiles emphasizing lifestyle positioning, design-forward assets, boutique scale, or independent collection experience.
archetypes.bestUseCase: May be relevant for lifestyle-positioned, boutique-scale, or design-forward hospitality assets under third-party or hybrid paths.
alignmentSignals: Potential alignment when chain scale, hotel type, or project type signals lifestyle or boutique positioning.
May be relevant if conversion or reflag pathways require experience-led operating models.
Alignment signal applies when the owner selected Independent / Boutique operator profile preference.
reviewConsiderations: Clarify independent collection path versus soft-brand or hard-brand affiliation.
Review F&B and experience programming intensity against operator lifestyle credentials.
Validate room count and staffing model for boutique economics.
questionsToClarify: Is the owner pursuing a collection, soft brand, or unbranded lifestyle path?
What guest experience and design standards must the owner confirm before outreach?
How much owner involvement is expected in brand and experience decisions?
dataGaps: No dedicated lifestyle boolean on deal intake; inference relies on chain scale, hotel type, and project type.
Operator lifestyle experience is not uniformly structured in setup records.
suggestedWorkflowActions: Suggested workflow action: confirm positioning (lifestyle vs. select-service) before lifestyle operator profile review.
Suggested workflow action: capture F&B and programming scope in deal notes.

archetypes.description: Profiles where the owner retains operating control while seeking selective commercial, revenue, or reporting support—not full hotel management.
archetypes.bestUseCase: May be relevant when the owner expects to remain operator-of-record with targeted commercial or revenue support only.
alignmentSignals: Potential alignment when preferred future operating model is owner-operated or franchise/license without full management.
May be relevant if services required exclude full management but include revenue, sales, or accounting support.
Alignment signal strengthens when commercial or yield priorities are elevated on the deal.
reviewConsiderations: Define scope boundaries to avoid gradual expansion into full management.
Review reporting cadence and owner approval rights for commercial decisions.
Validate incentive alignment when the owner retains P&L accountability.
questionsToClarify: Which functions must remain owner-controlled versus delegated?
Is any third-party management still under consideration alongside commercial support?
What reporting package does the owner require from a commercial partner?
dataGaps: No explicit owner retains operating control field; inferred from operating models and services.
Operator profiles rarely declare partial-service scope in structured multis.
suggestedWorkflowActions: Suggested workflow action: list required services explicitly and exclude full management if that is the owner intent.
Suggested workflow action: align commercial support scope with contract structure before outreach.

archetypes.description: Profiles aligned with brand-led operating standards, franchised or brand-managed structures, and defined brand compliance pathways.
archetypes.bestUseCase: May be relevant when the deal path assumes brand-led standards with a defined operator-of-record or brand-managed structure.
alignmentSignals: Potential alignment when preferred future operating model includes brand-managed or brand-plus-third-party paths.
May be relevant if the hotel is branded, considering brands, or conversion/reflag is in scope.
Alignment signal ties to brand portfolio and compliance themes—not a specific operator company in this phase.
reviewConsiderations: Clarify division of responsibilities between brand, owner, and operator-of-record.
Review PIP, brand standards, and conversion timeline assumptions.
Validate bid audience includes brands and operators as intended.
questionsToClarify: Is the owner pursuing franchise, management, or brand-managed agreement structure?
Which brand standards and PIP obligations are already modeled?
Who will be operator-of-record under the brand-managed structure?
dataGaps: Brand-managed path can overlap franchise-only paths on intake forms.
Profile-level output does not score brand-operator pairing.
suggestedWorkflowActions: Suggested workflow action: confirm brand-managed vs. third-party-only intent before operator profile review.
Suggested workflow action: validate PIP and standards assumptions with owner records.
